canvas.$description: Canvas — Page background, primary display surface.

graphite.$description: Graphite — Secondary surface, used for darker interactive states or background elements, often paired with lighter text.

ink.$description: Ink — Primary text color for maximum contrast, borders, and some background elements in high-contrast sections.

steel.$description: Steel — Muted text, subtle borders, and sometimes as a background fill for iconography or subtle navigation states.

smoke.$description: Smoke — Decorative borders around elements, muted text for secondary information.

electric-blue.$description: Electric Blue — Interactive elements, 'buy now' links, and accents. Its vividness draws attention to key actions.

verdant-accent.$description: Verdant Accent — Occasionally used for decorative fills, notably in SVG icons, less frequently for UI elements.

te-20.$description: General body text, navigation elements, links, and detailed product descriptions. The variety of thin weights keeps text light and airy.

te-40.$description: Headlines and prominent display text. The singular light weight (300) is a signature choice, creating an understated impact, making the text feel designed rather than shouted.

canvas.$description: Surface level 1: Primary page background, light canvases for product display.

graphite.$description: Surface level 2: Secondary background for navigation, footers, or sections intended to recede or provide contrast for lighter elements.

ink.$description: Surface level 3: High-contrast background for specific elements or headers within darker sections, providing maximum textual legibility against lighter content.
